Soup Joumou

Served at: Fete de Papa Zaka - Feast of the Farmer Loa

Serves 6-8Prep 30 minCook 1 hr 30 min

Soup Joumou is a traditional Haitian pumpkin soup celebrated on January 1st during the Fete de Papa Zaka, the Feast of the Farmer Loa. This hearty and flavorful soup symbolizes freedom and resilience, commemorating Haiti's independence and honoring the hardworking farmers.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups (960 ml) pumpkin or winter squash, peeled and cubed
  • 1 lb (450 g) beef stew meat, cut into chunks
  • 1 medium onion, chopped
  • 3 cloves garlic, minced
  • 2 stalks celery, chopped
  • 2 carrots, sliced
  • 1 medium potato, peeled and cubed
  • 1 cup (150 g) small pasta (like macaroni or vermicelli)
  • 1 Scotch bonnet pepper (whole, for flavor)
  • 2 sprigs fresh thyme
  • 1 bouquet garni (parsley, thyme, and bay leaf tied together)
  • 8 cups (1.9 L) beef broth or water
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) olive oil
  • Salt and black pepper to taste
  • 1 lime or lemon, juiced
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) evaporated milk or cream (optional)

Method

  1. In a large pot, heat olive oil over medium heat and brown the beef chunks on all sides.
  2. Add chopped onion, garlic, and celery to the pot and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
  3. Pour in the beef broth or water, then add the bouquet garni, thyme sprigs, and whole Scotch bonnet pepper.
  4. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 1 hour, or until the beef is tender.
  5. Remove the beef and set aside; discard the bouquet garni and Scotch bonnet pepper.
  6. Add the pumpkin, carrots, and potatoes to the broth and cook until tender, about 20 minutes.
  7. Using an immersion blender or regular blender, puree the soup until smooth and creamy.
  8. Return the beef to the pot, add the small pasta, and cook until the pasta is tender, about 10 minutes.
  9. Season with salt, black pepper, and lime or lemon juice to taste.
  10. Stir in evaporated milk or cream if using, and heat through without boiling.
  11. Serve hot, traditionally with crusty bread.

Tips

  • Keep the Scotch bonnet pepper whole to add flavor without too much heat; remove before serving.
  • Use a rich pumpkin or winter squash for the best flavor and color.
  • This soup is often made in large batches and tastes even better the next day.
